children: Japan’s monetary base contracted by 13.6% year-on-year in October 2026, marking the 15th consecutive month of decline, although the pace eased from a 15.2% drop in September.

The latest contraction was driven by a 16.4% fall in current account balances at the Bank of Japan, following an 18.3% decline in September, while banknotes in circulation fell 2.3% (vs. 2.0% in September) and coins in circulation eased 1.1% (vs. 1.2%).
Reserve balances also declined by 15.2%, compared with a 17.3% contraction a month earlier.
On an average outstanding basis, the monetary base stood at ¥532.6 trillion in October, slightly below ¥532.8 trillion in September.
Meanwhile, the seasonally adjusted annualized monthly growth rate turned positive at 4.9%, following a 10.2% decline in September.

title: Japan Monetary Base Declines for 15th Straight Month
